summary: The detached H training container ran to completion and exited 0, but the orchestrator that launched it was killed with its parent editor unit by systemd-oomd at 2026-11-16T01:24:08Z. No court receipt, log copy, run receipt or evaluation was written for H; the training artifacts are intact and the final checkpoint verifies.

orchestrator.why_no_progress_after_234516Z: the orchestrator was blocked in `scripts/court wait` (docker wait) on the detached container, which writes nothing until the container exits

host_pressure.cause: systemd-oomd killed the editor service that owned the orchestrator's process tree

2026-11-16T01:24:08Z systemd[1773]: app-dev.zed.Zed@4eb5e1a61f8e4269b3af932d9283f798.service: Consumed 2d 10h 58min 4.467s CPU time over 4d 6h 59min 38.492s wall clock time, 59.6G memory peak, 85.8G memory swap peak.
host_pressure.note: dmesg and the kernel journal carry no oom-kill entry for the training container; the kill was the cgroup-v2 userspace OOM killer acting on the editor unit, of which the orchestrator was a child process

training_container.name: selvedge-oracle-court-20261115T234515Z-b23ea1
training_container.container_memory_pressure: none recorded; the container exited 0 under its own 8 GiB limit
training_container.post_hoc_note: 8 GiB was the pre-S16 default for this armoury. S16 relaunches hybrid train/eval containers at SELVEDGE_MEM=24g per the operator directive; see the launch receipt.

recovery_decision: Do not rerun H training. Harvest the completed container with `scripts/court wait`, compose the run receipt from the verified checkpoint, then evaluate H with the registered harness.
code_fix: scripts/run-t2-pilot.sh gained a verified-final-checkpoint harvest path and per-stage state transitions so a host-process death between a finished checkpoint and its evaluation can be resumed without retraining
